name: Petroglyphs of the Archaeological Landscape of Tanbaly
description: Tucked into a green gorge in the dry Chu-Ili mountains, about 170 km northwest of Almaty, Tanbaly holds roughly 5,000 rock carvings spread across 48 clusters. The oldest were cut around 3,000 years ago in the Bronze Age, the latest in the early 1900s. Nearby you can see ancient graves and settlements, and the central canyon, with its densest carvings and apparent altars, was likely a place of sacrifice.
